summary: Request: guidance on configuring priority classes and threshold ladders for mixed realtime + bulk workloads
description: Issue summary: Customer runs a mixed workload from the same API key: low-latency websocket chat sessions plus large batch embedding imports. They recently changed the tenant's threshold ladder (burst credits and sustained window) to reduce cost, and since the change have seen a spike of 429 responses that look like tenant-level token exhaustion rather than per-route throttles. Impact: customer reports intermittent 429s that cause degraded UX for interactive sessions (timeouts, reconnects) and failed batch jobs. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1; single API key used by an orchestrator that fans out both chat and bulk workers. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start 150 concurrent websocket chat sessions, each sending short prompts every 1s. 2) Simultaneously start 10 parallel batch embedding jobs that submit 2k requests each over 10 minutes. 3) Observe tenant 429s on chat sessions after ~6 minutes; batch jobs see early failures and retries pile up. Logs / snippets: - ingress-rate-limiter [2026-03-10T14:21:04Z] token-window: tenant=Kestrel-99 available=0 refill_next=2026-03-10T14:22:00Z - gateway [2026-03-10T14:21:05Z] 429 POST /v1/embeddings 200ms xid=... reason=tenant_quota_exhausted - websocket-proxy [2026-03-10T14:21:08Z] disconnect user=chat-conn-73 code=429 message="rate limit exceeded" Additional context: Prior to ladder change they had a larger burst bucket and a longer sustained window. The customer changed two knobs: lowered burst_credits from 20000->6000 and reduced refill_smoothing_window from 60s->15s to reduce cost during quiet periods. They chose to keep routes unsegregated (chat + embeddings share same tenant quota).
investigation_notes: Checked tenant-level token accounting: counters show rapid token depletion when batch importer begins; chat sessions contribute smaller per-request tokens but high concurrency leads to additional counting due to websocket connection keepalive probes.
Observed refill alignment artifact: with smoothing_window reduced to 15s, burst drawdown followed by a slower apparent refill cadence causing periodic hard 429s between refill ticks.
No sign of a bug in gateway code path; rate-limiter logs show expected behavior given configured ladder but customer expectation was different (they expected route isolation to prevent chat impact).
Checked dedicated pool utilization: GPUs not saturated; this is quota accounting behavior rather than serving capacity exhaustion.
hypotheses: 1) Mixed workload is exhausting tenant burst credits because routes are not isolated; short high-concurrency chat spikes trigger repeated small token uses that, combined with batch job token usage, hit tenant window.
2) Shrinking smoothing_window created refill boundary effects (microbursts) that are leading to synchronized refill gaps across clients.
3) Health-check/keepalive probes are being counted towards tenant quota and amplify depletion under high connection counts.
mitigation_recommendations: Short-term (same day): advise customer to re-enable larger burst_credits to stop immediate 429s (recommended temporary setting: 20000) or throttle batch ingesters during peak interactive hours.

Medium-term (1-2 weeks): recommend enabling per-route quota separation so chat routes have their own token bucket with higher priority weight and a small dedicated burst (e.g., route_quota: chat=20% tenant, embeddings=70% tenant, background=10%).
Config examples: - route_quota.chat.weight=0.2 - route_quota.chat.burst=8000 - route_quota.embeddings.weight=0.7 - tenant.refill_smoothing_window=60s
Operational: enable transparent throttle headers (X-RateLimit-*) so clients can backoff more gracefully and implement splay on retry waves to avoid synchronized retries.
Long-term: if cost is a concern, use dynamic routing to send low-latency traffic to a small dedicated pool or priority lane with smaller instance count but reserved burst credits.

resolution: Temporary fix: reverted burst_credits and smoothing_window; immediate 429s for chat subsided. Permanent guidance provided: enable per-route quota separation, set priority weights, and use rate-limit headers + client-side jitter. Created internal task (INT-135800) to investigate auto-smoothing and keepalive accounting. Customer agreed to staged rollout of per-route quotas next week. Marking ticket as In Progress until route config is live and verified.
